notes:
Account background: Stalwart Capacity Solutions is a payments infrastructure provider with strict latency and residency needs. They run fraud scoring and realtime reranking during transaction flow; any tail latency >150ms for decision paths causes material revenue impact. They are evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace an internal GPU stack and to provide standardized rollout across EU and NA regions.

Requirements summary (from calls):
- Workloads: mixed (chat for ops assistant, real-time reranking for transaction flow, embeddings for search)
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 30ms (non-chat scoring), p95 < 120ms for reranking paths, hard tail target p99 < 250ms. Chat conversational flows acceptable up to p95 300ms for opportunistic features.
- Throughput / capacity: baseline sustained throughput expected ~40k tokens/min for scoring pipelines (equivalent to ~1,200 requests/min at average 30 tokens/request). Peak bursts up to 5x baseline during promotions/events.
- Reserved GPU planning: target reservation = 8x A100-equivalent GPUs in NA, 4x in EU to start. Want contract that allows predictable commit sizing with quarterly review for burst credits.
- Autoscaling policy preferences: aggressive scale-up on scheduled traffic spikes (scale within 30s target by pre-warming) and conservative scale-down to avoid cache churn (scale-down delay >=10 minutes). Prefer warm pool of pre-initialized replicas per model variant (nominal warm pool = 2 replicas) to keep KV cache & compiled kernels hot.
- Warm pools / cache: must persist KV caches for common prefixes (payment routing templates) and prefer pinned precompiled kernels for prioritized model variants. Warm pool should support instant routing (<50ms additional latency) when serving new connections.
- Queueing & admission: want bounded queueing with backpressure. If request queue exceeds 500ms wait, auto-fallback to cheaper quantized model (fallback model mapping to be defined) and/or degrade non-critical features. Require metrics for queue depth and per-route wait times.
- Batching behavior: prefer dynamic batching capped at 8 tokens for scoring flows to minimize latency; allow larger batch sizes for background embedding jobs. Need visibility into batch composition and per-batch latency contribution.
- SLA negotiation points: request credits for missed latency SLOs at p95 and p99 thresholds, clear definition of what constitutes 'downtime' during model rollouts, mandatory runbook for cross-region failover and warm pool rehydration.

POC plan:
- 72-hour soak on Redwood Dedicated pool (NA) with 1:1 production traffic replay + synthetic bursts simulating 5x traffic for 10-15min windows.
- Validate: sustained throughput (40k tokens/min), p95 and p99 latency targets, autoscaler scale-up time, scale-down timing impact on tail latency, warm pool effectiveness (cache hit rates vs cold starts).
- Success criteria: sustained baseline throughput within 5% of target, p95 latency within SLO for 95% of test windows, warm pool reduces cold starts by >80%, autoscaler responds within SLA for 90% of bursts.

Open action items / blockers:
- Procurement needs final pricing table and term sheet (legal flagged the model variant fallback and credits language).
- Network: on-prem VPC connectors require egress firewall rules approved by Stalwart net team (open).
- KMS: timeline for customer-managed keys unclear; need integration runbook and test account.

Key quotes from stakeholders:
- "Cost matters but if we can't guarantee tail behavior, the feature will be disabled and customers will notice." — Head of Payments
- "We need deterministic autoscaling during promotions; no surprises when traffic spikes." — Platform Lead

Suggested Redwood positioning for next call:
- Present explicit autoscaling policy templates (scale-up thresholds, buffer pool sizing, time-to-serve targets).
- Provide a short demo of warm-pool rehydration and quantized fallback in a sand-boxed traffic replay.
- Share a draft SLA appendix that ties latency SLOs to remediation credits and runbook steps.

References / stubs: pricing deck link + security FAQ already shared in Drive. POC ticket opened: INF-3121.
